data.summary: ddflow verify judges a done task against the CURRENT task_pipeline, not the pipeline at completion, so a task completed before the ci gate existed is reported [FAIL] gates never run and never skipped: ci and 'does not hold'. Eight of 21 BL-from-mining tasks (B22 B-parallel-tests B17 B23 B-cadence-phase-close B-docs-phase-gate B16 B26) FAIL on this alone: a false 'does not hold' (exit 1) buries real failures. R-verify-pipeline-retro CONFIRMED the mechanism on 2026-10-05 and no bug was ever filed. The completion ledger should store its pipeline, or verify should consult the gates configured at the completion time.
data.title: verify fails old completions for a gate added after they completed

data.summary: ddflow gate run <phase> unit_tests waited 31 minutes on the suite lock, ran, then printed 'unit_tests ran on e234caf3ce36, but the tree is now at 4fadc519c390: its outcome is superseded and was not recorded' and exited 3. The one commit between them is 'events: complete B-hot-files', which touches only .ddflow/events. services/gates/evidence.py superseded_by scopes by paths (the item's globs), and a phase has no globs, so ancestry alone decides (the B-e47bb1cade scoping does not reach phases). started_on is also taken before the suite-lock wait, so the queue time counts. The verdict and pytest counts are printed nowhere, so the run is lost. On a busy main a phase whole-suite gate may never be recordable. Event-only commits should not supersede, and a superseded run should still say what it found.
data.title: A phase's unit_tests outcome is thrown away by any commit, events-only ones included

data.body:

chunk_findings.detail: A capped `next --lane` still drops a selection flag the rerun must repeat. `_lane_token` is called with lane, kind, and phase only, while `next_lane` is also filtered by `phase_only`. Given `ddflow next --lane L --phase-only` (any kind/phase) whose answer is capped, the footer command has no `--phase-only`, so the named rerun is not the same selection — the same class of miss as the kind/phase bug this change claims to close.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite only loosens `len(...) <= chars // 2` to `<= chars` and retitles the truncation message from "wire half" to "budget". The `chars` setup and the 40-row fixture are unchanged, and that fixture was sized so three quarters of the body exceeds the *half* budget, not `max_chars`. With the intended full-budget contract, `assert "truncated" in body` fails even though the JSON is within `chars`. With the old half-budget still in place, both assertions still pass, so the test never shows that `--json status --by-tag` stopped cutting at `chars // 2`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_output_caps.py:test_status_by_tag_json_keeps_the_budget_of_plain_status

chunk_findings.detail: The slice drops the very token it then requires. Given `--explain` text `output.max_chars: … ASCII only; see output.non_ascii_weight\noutput.non_ascii_weight: …`, `block.index("output.non_ascii_weight")` cuts the pointer off, so `"non_ascii_weight" in block` is false even though the max_chars doc qualifies the 4-chars claim and points at that setting. The assertion only passes if `non_ascii_weight` is repeated before the qualified name.
